headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared file/MCP pathways; Semantic Kernel’s default networked plugin model can amplify unsafe outputs from a non-runnable content source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing source with no runtime surfaces, while Profile B can read/write files and use MCP. A cannot directly inject by itself, but if its content is placed into B’s workspace or plugin inputs, B may treat it as trusted. The pathway exists in default orchestration, though not proven directly.
conditions: IF Profile A content is copied into a file or MCP input consumed by Profile B
IF Profile B parses that content as instructions or tool directives without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all A-derived content before B ingests it
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text in B
Route A outputs through a human review step before B tool use
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile B can read/write filesystem and call external APIs, and it handles plugin credentials and application context. Profile A is a docs-only content source, so leakage is mainly from shared workspace or copied content into B’s context. The pair can expose sensitive application context if A-derived files are ingested by B and then sent to third-party services.
conditions: IF A-derived files contain sensitive material and are readable by B
IF B forwards that material to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Remove secrets from any files B can read
Restrict B’s outbound API targets to approved endpoints
Review plugin credentials before enabling B
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on B’s file and API paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile A has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Profile B can write files but cannot modify git state or spawn subprocesses. The only plausible conflict is shared application-defined files if A’s content is manually staged into B’s workspace; that is a limited write overlap, not a broad concurrency hazard.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF A-derived artifacts are edited by B while another process also writes them
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B
Lock shared files during B writes
Avoid using git-backed workflows for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around B

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile A can generate prompt-engineering content that B may ingest as application context or plugin instructions. Profile B’s agent/plugin pattern can then act on that input with external API access. Because B is not documented as verifying A’s outputs, A’s content can cascade into B’s actions or outputs in default workflows.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced text as authoritative context
IF B executes plugin calls or API requests based on that text without verification
mitigations: Require B to cite or validate A-derived claims before acting
Insert a review gate before any B tool call
Mark A outputs as untrusted input in B prompts
requires-engineering: add structured verification between A and B

E_compliance.rationale: Profile A is a docs-only open-source repository, so it does not itself create residency or retention obligations. Profile B handles application context and plugin credentials, which can create compliance issues if regulated data is routed through external model providers or MCP servers. The mismatch is conditional and narrower than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s application context
IF B sends that data to non-approved external providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Classify data before it enters B
Disable regulated-data workflows in B
Restrict B to approved providers only
Document retention and residency for B plugins
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data routing
